rule: Do not conflate diegetic story time, publication/edition time, and art-direction reference time. Each may inform different Items.

diegetic_story_time.current_interpretation: The frame narrative uses dates in the form 17—, and Victor's creation story occurs earlier than Walton's frame. Treat the world as late-18th-century unless a more precise episode decision is justified.
implications: Costume/technology/world objects should not automatically inherit 1818 or 1831 publication fashions.
Affects wording/source contract and can inform visual culture, but is not automatically the diegetic date.
References can teach line language, anatomy, composition or location even when their dates differ from the diegetic world; the difference must be deliberate and appropriate to the Item.

item_guidance.victor_costume: Prefer diegetic-time evidence first; compare later publication-era reinterpretation only as an explicit stylization alternative.
item_guidance.living_engraving_linework: May draw from early-19th-century engraving language because style-reference date and diegetic costume date are separate decisions.
item_guidance.apparatus: Validate against the technology/history required by the fictional event; do not infer exact apparatus from publication date alone.
